html:
SMTO-TSK-0037 — SMTO can't confirm or change your update to the task right now

GUID: 731e103a-87ee-4b6d-b5a3-80a53ab0b780
Slug: steering-state-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • Your update to the task may still be on its way or may already be in use, so SMTO can't promise it can be added, changed or withdrawn. The text you typed is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: look in the conversation for your update, or for a task reply that follows it. Sending it again could give the task the same instruction twice.
  2. If an earlier update is still being delivered, wait until it appears in the task before sending another update or deleting the task. SMTO holds new updates and deletion until the earlier update is delivered.
  3. If the task has finished or stopped, send your text as a new message instead of an update. A finished task can't take updates, and your text is still in the box.
  4. Only if your update clearly didn't reach a still-running task, select Steer (or Retry steer) again. This makes sure the task gets the instruction exactly once.

What success looks like

  • Your update shows once in the conversation as sent, applied or cancelled, and the task carries on.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep pressing Cancel or resending the update to undo it; that can't take back an update the task has already used.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Steering or steer cancellation was refused or unconfirmed: the run is no longer steering-eligible, an earlier amendment is still being delivered (which also blocks task deletion), or the amendment was already claimed or applied and cannot be withdrawn.

What this means

  • Steering requires an eligible active run and no conflicting pending delivery. Withdrawal additionally requires the exact retained submission and an amendment not yet claimed or applied. A missing cancellation acknowledgement does not establish whether the instruction was withdrawn or consumed. Inspect the original submission receipt and run state before choosing another control; this diagnostic adds no cancellation or execution.

Why this can happen

  • The run cannot accept steering, its delivery remains pending, or withdrawal cannot match an unclaimed retained amendment.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact submission receipt, current run status and whether the amendment is already claimed or applied.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the run snapshot and the original amendment's receipt (amendment_seq) to see whether it is queued, applied or withdrawn; a missing cancellation acknowledgement does not establish whether the instruction was withdrawn or consumed. Use only controls still offered, and do not resubmit the instruction to resolve an uncertain cancellation.
  • Refresh the original submission receipt and current run state. Use only the controls still available; do not resubmit the instruction to resolve an uncertain cancellation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Reconcile the original instruction and withdrawal receipt before resubmitting intent or choosing another control.

How to verify the fix

  • The original instruction has a confirmed queued, applied or withdrawn state under its exact submission identity.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • A rejected or unconfirmed cancellation does not prove the original instruction was never processed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
